wu: Review Relay Race: Teams race to write 10 jobs on the board. Teacher shouts 'Teacher! Doctor! Farmer!' and students run to write them. Winners get 2 points, others 1.
wuAlt: Job Charades: Students act out jobs like 'bake bread' or 'drive a bus' while others guess.
Flashcard Speed: Show job flashcards fast; teams shout the job name.
pres: Teacher shows realia (doctor's coat, chef's hat) and asks 'What is it? It is a __.' Then models 'What does a doctor do? They help people.' Students repeat in pairs with flashcards.
presAlt: Job Poster: Point to a poster of jobs and ask 'What does a farmer do? They grow food.' Students answer in full sentences.
Storytime: Read 'Jobs Around Us' story, stopping to ask 'What does the baker do?'
prac: Jobs Guessing Game: Team A thinks of a job, Team B asks 'Does it wear a hat? Do they work outside?' until they guess. Teacher monitors for full sentences like 'Yes, they do.'
pracAlt: Job Match-Up: Students match picture cards to job description cards ('They teach students.') in pairs.
TPR Job Actions: Teacher says 'Be a farmer!' and students pretend to plant seeds; 'Be a doctor!' and they pretend to check a patient.
ls: Listen and Circle: Students listen to audio of 5 jobs (e.g., 'A firefighter puts out fires.') and circle the correct picture on their worksheet. Teacher checks answers together.
re: Job Action Freeze: Play music; students dance to a job action (e.g., 'sweep like a cleaner'). When music stops, they freeze. Last one out sits down.
prod: Thank-You Cards: Students draw a worker they know (e.g., 'My father is a mechanic.') and write 'Thank you for working hard!' with crayons. They share with the class.
rw: Read and Match: Students read 3 simple sentences ('A teacher works at school.') and match them to the correct job picture. Then they trace 3 sentences about their dream job.
st: Read 'The Little Worker' story about a child helping at home. Sing 'What Do You Do?' song with actions. Goodbye routine: Goodbye Song + sticker chart + high-five line.
g: Teams take turns running to write a job on the board; no duplicates allowed.
Teacher describes a job ('I wear a uniform and drive a bus.'); students guess.
Students draw a job for their team to guess.
Students act out jobs while others guess the name.
Students mark off jobs called by the teacher.
diff: Fast finishers: Write 5 sentences about what jobs they want to do when they grow up.
Support: Trace the job names and match to pictures with sentence starters.
hw: Draw one job you love and write 3 sentences about it (e.g., 'I love teachers. They help students. They are smart.')
Ask your family about their jobs and write them down.
Play the Jobs Guessing Game with your family.
tip: Use Moroccan context: highlight local jobs like 'artisan' or 'fisherman' to connect Labour Day to students' lives. Praise effort, not just correctness, during assessment.
checklist: I can name 10 jobs in English
I can ask 'What does a ___ do?'
I can listen and circle the correct job
I can read and match jobs to sentences
I can write 3 sentences about a job
I can say thank you to workers
